questions.stem: What are the four Ts that cause an anterior mediastinal mass?
Which structures can an anterior mediastinal mass compress, and what else can it cause?
questions.answer: Airway, great vessels (SVC obstruction), heart; also pleural effusion

questions.stem: Which three risk categories classify anterior mediastinal mass patients for anaesthesia?
What two items should be on standby for anterior mediastinal mass anaesthesia?
In thoracic anatomy, where is the mediastinum located?
questions.answer: The space between the two pleural cavities, from thoracic inlet to diaphragm

questions.stem: In the mediastinum, which plane divides it into superior and inferior parts?
options: Transpyloric plane, a horizontal line at L1
Costal margin line at the tenth rib
Thoracic plane, horizontal line from the sternal angle (T4)
Sagittal line through the midclavicular point

questions.stem: In the mediastinum, what does the superior compartment contain?
questions.answer: Thymus, aortic arch, SVC, areolar tissue, lymph nodes

questions.stem: Besides the 4Ts, which other mediastinal structures can give rise to a mass?
questions.answer: Trachea and bronchi, heart and pericardium, great vessels, oesophagus, spine

questions.stem: How is a diagnostic biopsy of an anterior mediastinal mass usually taken?
How is therapeutic resection of an anterior mediastinal mass performed?
Which unrelated emergency operations can occur in a patient with an anterior mediastinal mass?
When do anterior mediastinal mass effects often worsen?
questions.answer: When supine, after induction or after paralysis

questions.stem: What is compression of the trachea and bronchi by an anterior mediastinal mass called?
Which vascular complication can an anterior mediastinal mass cause?
What cardiovascular events can an anterior mediastinal mass cause, and when?
questions.answer: Hypotension or arrest after lying flat, induction or paralysis

questions.stem: What airway problem can vagus nerve compression by an anterior mediastinal mass cause?
Besides the airway, an anterior mediastinal mass can cause ____ compression.
What can pericardial invasion by an anterior mediastinal mass cause?
What does pleural invasion by an anterior mediastinal mass typically cause?
How do general anaesthesia and paralysis affect an anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Worsen compression of airway and vessels

questions.stem: What does IPPV do to an anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Raises intrathoracic pressure and worsens compression

questions.stem: What tools stratify the risk of airway or cardiovascular collapse under GA in anterior mediastinal mass?
What should be avoided in anterior mediastinal mass to keep spontaneous ventilation?
How should the effect of exercise and posture be graded in anterior mediastinal mass?
What determines the rescue position in anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Where the mass sits relative to the compressed structure

questions.stem: What does a PA and lateral chest X-ray show in anterior mediastinal mass?
Which investigation is the key test for anterior mediastinal mass?
How long does the CT scan for anterior mediastinal mass take?
For anterior mediastinal mass CT, the head and chest can be raised ____ degrees without spoiling the scan.
Which test is used for vascular compression symptoms or suspected effusion in anterior mediastinal mass?
Which lung function test is especially useful in anterior mediastinal mass, and in what positions?
Which tests help assess myasthenia as an underlying disease in anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Tensilon test or acetylcholine receptor antibodies

questions.stem: Which presentation features predict perioperative respiratory complications in anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Cardiorespiratory symptoms or signs at presentation

questions.stem: What CT tracheal diameter predicts higher perioperative respiratory risk in anterior mediastinal mass?
In anterior mediastinal mass, a lung function PEFR below ____ predicts perioperative respiratory complications.
Which lung function pattern predicts perioperative respiratory complications in anterior mediastinal mass?
Which specialists should be involved in optimising anterior mediastinal mass patients before surgery?
questions.answer: Thoracic and ENT surgeons, medical and radiation oncology

questions.stem: For a high-risk anterior mediastinal mass with a chemosensitive tumour, what should be considered first?
What is a drawback of giving chemotherapy or radiotherapy before surgery in anterior mediastinal mass?
In anterior mediastinal mass with suspected tracheal obstruction, what premedication should be avoided?
Which risk category applies to CT tracheal or bronchial diameter > 50% of normal in anterior mediastinal mass?
Which risk category applies to an asymptomatic adult with CT tracheal diameter < 50% of normal?
Which risk category applies to a symptomatic child with CT tracheal diameter > 50% of normal?
Which risk category applies to a child with CT tracheal diameter < 50% of normal?
Which invasive line is placed before induction in anterior mediastinal mass?
Where should IV access go in anterior mediastinal mass with SVC obstruction?
For anterior mediastinal mass, what induction position may some patients need?
What is the first airway option for anterior mediastinal mass?
What is the second airway option for anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Asleep and cardiostable, keeping spontaneous breathing until the airway is secure or the case is done

questions.stem: In anterior mediastinal mass, what does ketamine do to FRC during spontaneous breathing?
In anterior mediastinal mass under ketamine, what does better rib cage tone prevent?
questions.answer: The diaphragm moving cephalad, which may prevent mass-related obstruction

questions.stem: For PA or cardiac compression in anterior mediastinal mass, how should induction be done?
Who should be present with the rigid bronchoscope at induction in anterior mediastinal mass?
Why are the patient draped and surgeons scrubbed before induction in anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: For immediate sternotomy and lifting the mass off

questions.stem: Before induction, what elective support should be considered for anterior mediastinal mass?
For anterior mediastinal mass, how long does cannulation and establishing bypass flow take, even with a primed pump?
In anterior mediastinal mass emergencies, what step restores spontaneous breathing?
After waking an anterior mediastinal mass patient in an emergency, where is the patient moved?
Which emergency surgical step is taken for anterior mediastinal mass compressing the great vessels?
questions.answer: Immediate sternotomy and lifting the mass off the great vessels

questions.stem: What emergency airway step is taken to ventilate an anterior mediastinal mass patient?
In anterior mediastinal mass, what can be placed under vision after ventilating through a rigid bronchoscope?
During anterior mediastinal mass surgery, what should be watched for, for example during surgical handling?
Which complication should be watched for in anterior mediastinal mass, especially with SVC obstruction?
How should a patient with anterior mediastinal mass be extubated?
What device should be considered at extubation in anterior mediastinal mass?
After anterior mediastinal mass surgery, what is the minimum level of postoperative care?
Why do children with anterior mediastinal mass present with obstruction earlier?
questions.answer: A small fall in tracheal diameter causes a large fall in area and rise in resistance

questions.stem: For VATS excision of a thymoma in a safe anterior mediastinal mass patient, what position is used?
questions.answer: Supine, body tilted to one side, arms by the side

questions.stem: In thymoma VATS excision, which side is the machine brought in from?
Why are back supports needed for VATS excision in anterior mediastinal mass?
questions.answer: Patients tend to roll backwards more than in routine lung surgery
